verdict.winner: Metal roofing wins on lifespan; asphalt shingles win on upfront NJ cost.
verdict.reasoning: Choose metal roofing over asphalt shingles when the roof stays 40+ years. Metal's 40-80-year life (InterNACHI) spreads its higher $9.00-$16.00 NJ per-square-foot cost across 2-4 asphalt lifecycles, lowering cost per year of service.
verdict.alternate: Asphalt shingles win when upfront budget or resale timing leads. Asphalt installs at $5.50-$11.00 per NJ square foot (Josten Roofing) and recoups ~61% of job cost at resale versus metal's ~49%, per the Remodeling/Zonda 2023 Cost vs Value report.

keyFacts: Metal roofing lasts 40-80 years versus asphalt shingles' 20-30 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart.
Asphalt 3-tab shingles last about 20 years and architectural (laminated) asphalt about 30 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart.
Copper metal roofing exceeds 70 years of service life, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart.
Asphalt shingles install at $5.50-$11.00 per NJ square foot versus metal roofing at $9.00-$16.00+ per NJ square foot, per Josten Roofing.
Within asphalt, 3-tab installs at $5.50-$9.50 and architectural at $6.50-$11.00 per NJ square foot, per Josten Roofing.
Labor accounts for roughly 60% of an asphalt roofing project cost, per HomeGuide.
A full NJ asphalt-shingle roof replacement falls within $10,000-$25,000, while a metal roof replacement falls in the upper half of that range or higher.
Asphalt repair runs $150-$500 for a shingle and $400-$1,000 for a valley; metal repair runs $150-$1,000 for a fastener issue and up to $3,000 for a corrosion leak.
Asphalt shingles hold snow until it melts, while metal roofing sheds snow and therefore needs snow guards over entryways.
An asphalt roof replacement recoups ~61% of job cost at resale versus ~49% for a metal roof, per the Remodeling/Zonda 2023 Cost vs Value report.
A new asphalt roof adds roughly $15,247 to resale value on a typical home and lets sellers ask 1%-3% more, per Opendoor and Zillow 2025 analysis.
A reflective roof stays over 50 degrees F cooler than a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon, per the U.S. Department of Energy.
Reflective roofing is rated by solar reflectance and thermal emittance (not R-value), per the Cool Roof Rating Council.
A cool/reflective roof cuts peak cooling demand 11-27% in air-conditioned homes, per the EPA.
Newark sits in heating-dominated Climate Zone 4A-5, so reflective-roof cooling savings carry a winter heating offset, per the DOE.
Asphalt shingles reach reflective performance through reflective-granule product lines, a lower-cost path to the same reflectance-and-emittance levers, per the EPA and CRRC.
Newark averages 31.5 inches of annual snowfall, with roughly 78% falling December-February, per NOAA 1991-2020 normals.
Northern NJ roofs face roughly 35-45 freeze-thaw cycles each winter, stressing both asphalt and metal systems.
Northern NJ has a design wind speed of roughly 110-115 mph under ASCE 7-16, per ASCE wind maps; metal panels resist that uplift while shed snow still requires snow guards, per NRCA guidance.
Asphalt shingles depend on an ice-and-water barrier at the eaves to block ice-dam backup and lose protective granules under hail, degrading faster under UV than metal, per NRCA and ARMA guidance.

Metal roofing resists hail better than asphalt: hail dents thin panels without breaching weatherproofing, while asphalt loses granules that accelerate UV degradation, per NRCA and ARMA guidance; impact-rated shingles narrow the gap.

Metal roofing installed over solid decking and underlayment is no louder than asphalt shingles in rain; the 'tin roof' noise comes from agricultural panels on open framing without a deck beneath, per the gold source context.
Metal roofing installs over one existing asphalt-shingle layer in many NJ cases, though deck condition governs whether the overlay is sound.

njContext: The NJ Uniform Construction Code treats a full re-roof of asphalt shingles or metal roofing as ordinary maintenance on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling, requiring no permit, inspection, or notice, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and the NJ DCA 2018 alert.

A NJ UCC permit is required once roof work turns structural (replacing rafters, trusses, or ridge beams) or exceeds 25% of roof area within 12 months on commercial, condo, or attached buildings, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b) and 5:23-2.7(c).
A NJ full asphalt-shingle roof replacement falls within $10,000-$25,000; a metal roof replacement falls in the upper half of that range or higher.
Newark averages 31.5 inches of annual snowfall (~78% December-February) per NOAA 1991-2020 normals, and northern NJ roofs see roughly 35-45 freeze-thaw cycles per winter.
Metal roofing's snow shedding adds snow guards over Newark entryways, while asphalt shingles rely on an ice-and-water barrier at the eaves against ice-dam backup, per NOAA normals and NRCA guidance.
Architectural asphalt offers the widest color and profile range for color-and-budget-driven Essex County homes, while metal suits long-hold owners with its 40-80-year life, per the InterNACHI chart.

Metal roofing on a commercial building triggers a NJ UCC permit once roof work exceeds 25% of roof area in 12 months, since the ordinary-maintenance exemption covers only detached 1- and 2-family dwellings, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(c).

Asphalt shingles install faster on commercial steep-slope sections (shorter tenant disruption); metal's panel-and-trim fabrication extends the install window in exchange for decades of lower-maintenance service, per NRCA installation guidance.
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (registration under the NJ Consumer Fraud Act, N.J.S.A. 56:8-136 — NOT a roofing license, which NJ does not issue), insured, offering a free written estimate. NQR installs both asphalt shingles and metal roofing and recommends the material that fits the specific Essex County home, budget, and ownership horizon. Frame warranties honestly as two separate parts: the manufacturer's limited material/system warranty (set and registered by the maker, e.g. GAF for asphalt or Englert/ATAS/McElroy Metal for metal) and NQR's own written workmanship warranty — never present manufacturer certification tiers (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc.) as NQR credentials. No solar/ITC content applies to this comparison.

buyersGuide.h1: Which Is Better: Asphalt Shingles vs Metal Roofing?
buyersGuide.directAnswerThesis: Metal roofing is better for the long hold, lasting 40-80 years versus asphalt's 20-30 (InterNACHI); asphalt is better for upfront budget and near-term resale, installing cheaper and recouping ~61% versus metal's ~49%.

expertPicks.directAnswerThesis: The standards favor metal for longevity (40-80 years, InterNACHI) and asphalt for budget and resale; match material to ownership horizon, verify a registered NJ Home Improvement Contractor, and weigh manufacturer plus written workmanship warranties.
